title: Company-wide policies and processes — access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Consolidated company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and reusable internal templates.
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and associated processes for operational consistency and audit readiness. It is intended for all staff, managers, and contractors. It defines high-level principles, concrete procedures, approval matrices, and reusable templates for common actions (access requests, change rollouts, procurement, vendor onboarding, travel & expenses).

Scope

Applies to: all employees, contingent workers, contractors, and any third party with access to Redwood systems or data.
Exclusions: team-level process variations that have documented exceptions approved by the relevant policy owner and Security/People Ops.

Policy owner and governance

- Primary owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel)
- Security owner (controls related to authentication/authorization): Security & Compliance (Sofia Alvarez)
- Finance owner (procurement/expenses): Finance (Jordan Lee)
- Change & Release coordination: Eng SRE (Carlos Gomez)

Policies are reviewed at least annually and after any major regulatory or product changes. Review schedule: People Ops owns the calendar; reviewers listed in metadata are required for sign-off on substantive updates.

1) Access and permissions

Principles
- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based access for systems where feasible.
- Time-bound elevated access when needed (temporary admin access).
- Segregation of duties for sensitive operations (billing, key management, prod deploys).

Access request workflow (standard)
1. Employee or manager submits request via internal access portal / ticket (Jira project: ACCESS). Include justification, requested duration, and owner approval.
2. Manager approval required for most role assignments. For privileged roles (see table below), Security must review and approve.
3. Access provisioned by the system owner (engineer/SRE) or IAM automation; requester notified.
4. All temporary elevated access automatically expires after the approved period; renewals require a repeat request.

Access levels (summary table)
| Level | Typical roles | Approvers | Review cadence | Controls |
|-------|---------------|----------|----------------|----------|
| Viewer | Read-only dashboards, non-sensitive configs | Manager | Quarterly | MFA required |
| Editor | Deploys to non-prod, edit configs | Manager + Service Owner | Monthly | MFA, audit logging |
| Admin | Provisioning, account management | Manager + Security | 90 days (recertify) | MFA + SSO, 2-person approval for critical ops |
| Billing | Billing console, invoices | Finance + Exec | Quarterly | Justified access, restricted IP ranges |

Periodic recertification
- Service owners receive monthly recertification reminders. All accounts are audited quarterly by Security. Exceptions must be logged and approved by Security lead.

Emergency access (break glass)
- Break-glass accounts exist for on-call SREs and Security. Use requires an incident ticket, and all actions are logged and reviewed within 72 hours.

2) Change management (applies to infra, runtime, and customer-facing services)

Goals: ensure predictable rollouts, minimize service impact, preserve rollback capability, and maintain audit trail.

Change classification
- Major: schema changes, model-weight replacements, infra upgrades that may affect availability. Require Change Advisory Board (CAB) approval and a scheduled maintenance window.
- Minor: config updates, small code deploys with feature flags. Require automated tests and peer review.
- Emergency: hotfixes to mitigate active incidents. Follow emergency change process (post-change review required).

Standard change process (non-emergency)
1. Create a Change Request (CR) with details: description, owner, impact, rollback plan, test plan, schedule. Use template: `CHANGE-REQUEST-YYYYMMDD` (stored in Templates).
2. Automated gating: unit/integration tests, canary deployment tests, and performance regression checks (see Performance Standards).
3. For Major changes, present to CAB at least 72 hours prior to window. CAB includes Eng leads, SRE, Product, Security, and Finance as needed.
4. Execute during approved window; monitor SLOs and error budgets.
5. Post-change review within 3 business days, include rollback rationale if used.

Approval matrix (procurement-ish style applied to changes)
- Minor changes: Service owner approval + automated CI pass.
- Major changes (<$RISK threshold): CAB approval + Product sign-off.
- Major changes (high-risk): Executive sponsor + Security sign-off + Finance notification.

3) Data management and classification

Data classification levels
- Public: information intended for public consumption. No special handling.
- Internal: company-internal docs, non-sensitive logs. Access limited to employees.
- Confidential: PII (limited), model training data that is not customer-owned, product roadmaps. Access limited to specific teams and requires NDA where applicable.
- Restricted: customer-controlled data, regulated data (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR sensitive personal data), encryption keys, secrets. Access only to named individuals; logged and audited.

Handling requirements by class
- Storage: Restricted and Confidential data must be stored in approved systems with encryption at rest and in transit.
- Transmission: Use company-approved secure channels (VPN, SSO-backed apps).
- Retention: Follow Data Retention Policy (see related pages). Default retention windows: logs 90 days, non-sensitive backups 180 days, customer data per contract.
- Deletion: Data subject requests or contract-terms deletions are initiated via ticket to Data Ops and must follow secure wipe procedures.

Data access request and approval
1. Submit Data Access Form (Form stored in Templates). Include purpose, data scope, and duration.
2. Data owner review and approval; Security reviews high-scope requests.
3. Access provisioned with explicit audit logging enabled.

Data breach & incident handling
- Follow Incident Response (security) runbook. Notify Legal and People Ops within 24 hours of suspected exfiltration. Preserve forensic artifacts; do not rebuild systems before consent from Security.

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement principles
- Centralize vendor contracts through Finance.
- Prefer AWS Marketplace / cloud marketplace where supported for managed billing.
- Purchase commitments >$50k require Legal review and VP-level approval.

Procurement workflow
1. Requester completes Purchase Request (PR) template (Templates). Include business justification, budget code, and preferred vendor terms.
2. Manager approval for requests <$5k. For $5k–$50k, Finance manager approval required. >$50k requires Legal + Exec approval.
3. For SaaS or cloud services that will access company data, include Security review.
4. Finance issues PO or credit-card provisioning. Treasury maintains vendor payment terms.

Expense reimbursement (travel & misc)
- Employees submit expenses in the company expense system with receipts attached within 30 days.
- Per diem: $75 / day domestic; $150 / day international (exceptions require approval).
- Approval chain: direct manager -> Finance reviewer. Fraud or policy violations escalate to People Ops.

Cardholder policy
- Corporate cards require manager nomination and Finance approval. Card limits assigned based on role and expected spend. Card use is logged and reconciled monthly.

5) Vendor management and onboarding

Vendor segmentation
- Low risk: standard SaaS (no access to Restricted data).
- Medium risk: vendors with limited access to Internal/Confidential data.
- High risk: vendors handling Restricted data or running customer workloads.

Onboarding checklist (minimum)
1. Business justification and owner assignment.
2. Security questionnaire for vendors (Security reviews medium/high risk).
3. Contract with data processing addenda (DPA) if vendor will process customer data. Legal must review.
4. PO or contract executed; Finance configures payment terms.
5. Technical onboarding: set up accounts, role-limited service accounts, scoped API keys, logging endpoints.
6. Quarterly vendor review for medium/high risk vendors.

Offboarding
- Terminate credentials, revoke API keys, collect final invoices, ensure data return or secure deletion per contract, and perform an offboarding checklist documented in the vendor record.

6) Travel policy (business travel & safety)

Booking and approvals
- Travel must be pre-approved by manager and budget owner. Use the corporate travel portal.
- Preferred classes: economy for flights under 5 hours, premium economy for 5–9 hours (exceptions require Exec approval).

Expenses and reimbursement
- Submit itemized receipts; corporate card use preferred. Per diem rules apply (see Procurement and expenses).
- Lodging: prefer mid-tier business hotels; avoid long-term residential stays without approval.

Safety and incident reporting
- For international travel, register trip with People Ops. In case of safety incidents, notify People Ops and Security immediately. Travel insurance details are available via People Ops.

7) Internal templates and examples

Templates live in Templates library (Confluence & shared drive). Key templates referenced here:
- CHANGE-REQUEST-YYYYMMDD (change request template)
- ACCESS-REQUEST (access request form)
- DATA-ACCESS-FORM (data access request)
- PURCHASE-REQUEST (procurement/PO template)
- VENDOR-ONBOARDING-CHECKLIST
- EXPENSE-REIMBURSEMENT (expense submission template)

Example CLI snippet for emergency access revocation
```
# Revoke temporary role binding for user
gcloud iam roles remove-binding --role=roles/temporary_admin --member=user:alice@redwood.ai --project=redwood-infra
# Log in ticket system: ACCESS-1234
```

Audit, compliance and reporting
- Security and Finance coordinate an annual audit of access, procurement spend above thresholds, and vendor contracts.
- Monthly dashboards track open access requests, change rollouts, and outstanding procurement approvals.

Exceptions and waivers
- Temporary exceptions must be requested via Exception Request template, include a compensating control, and be approved by People Ops + Security. Permanent waivers require Exec sign-off and an entry in the Risk & Exceptions register.

Change log
- 2026-03-04: Document created (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-06-15: Added vendor segmentation and procurement thresholds (Jordan Lee).
- 2026-12-01: Expanded change management approval matrix and updated per diem (People Ops).

Where to get help
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (policy questions, exceptions)
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.ai (access, breach, vendor security)
- Finance: finance@redwood.ai (procurement, cards, expense reimbursements)
- Eng SRE (change coordination): eng-sre@redwood.ai

Appendices
A. Quick reference approval matrix (summary)
- <$5k: Manager
- $5k–$50k: Finance manager + Manager
- >$50k: Finance + Legal + Exec sponsor

B. Definition of roles and acronyms
- SRE: Site Reliability Engineering
- DPA: Data Processing Agreement
- CAB: Change Advisory Board
